Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

hep-ph.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
hep-ph.author: Tian-Nuo Li, William Giarè, Guo-Hong Du, Eleonora Di Valentino, Luis A. Anchordoqui, Shao-Jiang Wang, Xin Zhang, Rong-Gen Cai
hep-ph.abstract: In $\Lambda$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $\phi$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(\phi)\propto e^{-\beta\phi/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2\sigma$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.

hep-ph.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
hep-ph.author: Andrea Valletta, Francesco Crescimbeni, Takuya Katagiri, Francesco Pannarale, Paolo Pani
hep-ph.abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

hep-ph.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Top Taggers from JetClass to a Full-Simulation $Z'\to t\bar{t}$ Search: Transfer, Extrapolation, Sensitivity and Inference Cost
hep-ph.author: Manisha Kumari, Amal Sarkar
hep-ph.abstract: Searches for heavy resonances decaying to \(t\bar{t}\) test physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale, and their reach depends on how well boosted top jets are identified. Machine-learning top taggers are usually compared on fast-simulation samples without pileup and in a narrow jet-\(p_T\) window, so a benchmark ranking does not directly show how much each tagger adds to a real search. This study trains seven taggers under identical conditions on JetClass. They are a boosted decision tree, two image-based networks, ParticleNet, and three particle transformers (ParT, UParT, and GloParT). The taggers are then applied without retraining to a \(Z'\to t\bar{t}\) search with \(m_{Z'}\) between 1.2 and 2.5~TeV, using 2016 CMS Open Data simulated with Geant4 and realistic pileup. The overall benchmark order of the taggers is preserved. However, taggers with similar area under the ROC curve (AUC) differ by up to a factor of three in jet-level discovery significance. The particle transformers extend the mass reach of the search by \(400~\mathrm{GeV}\), and their lead grows with resonance mass. This gain is seen in fully merged top jets and is associated with stable performance at jet \(p_T\) above the training range. Pileup has only a minor effect on all taggers. A small convolutional network achieves competitive discrimination at a much lower computational cost. The gaps between tagger groups hold under retraining and within statistical uncertainties. The results show that a tagger must be chosen on its kinematic coverage, the working point of the analysis, its discovery sensitivity and its cost, and not on its benchmark score alone.

hep-ph.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
hep-ph.author: André A. Costa, Valdir B. Bezerra
hep-ph.abstract: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

hep-ph.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
hep-ph.author: Chan Youn Weon, Carsten van de Bruck, C.P. Burgess, Jeong Han Kim, Adam Smith
hep-ph.abstract: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.

hep-ph.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
hep-ph.author: Xingang Chen, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu
hep-ph.abstract: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.

hep-ph.title: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
hep-ph.author: Fengwei Yang, Kylar Greene, Aurora Ireland, Yuhsin Tsai
hep-ph.abstract: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.

hep-ph.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
hep-ph.author: Marco Calzà, Andrea Spina
hep-ph.abstract: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

hep-ph.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
hep-ph.author: Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Nikolas Cruz-Camacho, Rajesh Kumar, Veronica Dexheimer, Jaquelyn Noronha-Hostler
hep-ph.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

hep-ph.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
hep-ph.author: Aalok Misra, Shivam S. Kushwah, Keshav Dasgupta, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon
hep-ph.abstract: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio \zeta_\parallel/\eta_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available \zeta_\parallel/s, \eta_\parallel/s plots.

hep-ph.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
hep-ph.author: Shuntaro Aoki, Zhehan Qin, Masahide Yamaguchi, Yuhang Zhu
hep-ph.abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.

hep-ph.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
hep-ph.author: Karim Benakli
hep-ph.abstract: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.

hep-ph.title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
hep-ph.author: Xiangrun Bao, Lingxiao Wang, Huichao Song
hep-ph.abstract: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $\tau-\tau_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $\tau-\tau_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.

hep-ph.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
hep-ph.author: Zhengwen Liu
hep-ph.abstract: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $\eta$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.

hep-ph.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
hep-ph.author: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang
hep-ph.abstract: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.

hep-ph.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
hep-ph.author: Michael Leyton, Stephen T. Dye
hep-ph.abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW.Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

hep-ph.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
hep-ph.author: H. C. Das, J. B. Wei
hep-ph.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

hep-ph.title: Gauge Theory Bootstrap with varying $N_c$
hep-ph.author: Rafael Cordoba, Yifei He, Martin Kruczenski, Derek Ping, Jignesh Mohanty, Emil Alegria
hep-ph.abstract: We use the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study asymptotically free gauge theories with a varying number of colors $N_c$. The parameter $N_c$ enters the computation through the sum rules and asymptotic form factors, allowing us to tune this microscopic parameter directly and examine the corresponding low-energy strongly coupled dynamics. For $3\le N_c\le 12$, we extract the scattering lengths, effective ranges, and low-energy constants $\bar{l}_i$, and study their $N_c$ dependence. We also obtain the $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $f_2$ resonances for the same range of $N_c$. The $\rho$ and $f_2$ masses depend only weakly on $N_c$, and their widths decrease as $N_c$ increases, consistent with the $1/N_c$ scaling expected for conventional $q\bar{q}$ mesons. In contrast, the $\sigma$ meson mass and width both increase with $N_c$, in agreement with a previous unitarized $\chi$PT analysis. These results provide a further test of the Gauge Theory Bootstrap for studying asymptotically free gauge theories.

hep-ph.title: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
hep-ph.author: Stanislaw Mrowczynski, Maciej Pylak
hep-ph.abstract: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

hep-ph.title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
hep-ph.author: Ashish Pandav, Zhangbu Xu, Bedangadas Mohanty
hep-ph.abstract: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

hep-ph.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
hep-ph.author: Jinzi Wu, Michael Döring, Maxim Mai
hep-ph.abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

hep-ph.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
hep-ph.author: Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Isabelle S. Goldstein
hep-ph.abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

hep-ph.title: The Higgs boson as a self-similar system: Tsallis form factors and the electroweak hierarchy problem
hep-ph.author: M. Ahmadvand
hep-ph.abstract: We study the electroweak hierarchy problem for a composite Higgs boson with a statistically self-similar internal structure. Using the spectral representation of the Higgs propagator, we show that this structure can contribute only through momentum-dependent vertex functions. In a superstatistical model of the self-similar structure, a Gamma-distributed size of the constituents turns a Gaussian vertex form factor into the $q$-exponential (Tsallis) form factor $F_q(k_E^2)=[1+(q-1)k_E^2/M^2]^{-1/(q-1)}$, where $M$ is the compositeness scale and $q-1=2/(3N)$ for an effective number $N$ of constituents. These form factors interpolate between those of nonlocal field theories ($q\to1$) and Lee--Wick-type models ($q=2$). For $1<q<2$ every one-loop contribution to the Higgs mass is finite and heavy states decouple. For the benchmarks $q=11/9$, $4/3$ and $5/3$, tuning is negligible ($\Delta\lesssim1$) for $M$ up to about $1$--$2$~TeV, and remains mild ($\Delta \leq 10$) for $M$ up to about $3$--$5$~TeV. The hierarchy problem is thus converted into the requirement of new composite dynamics near the TeV scale, testable at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider through off-shell and high-momentum Higgs processes and searches for new states near $M$.

hep-ph.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
hep-ph.author: S.V. Troitsky
hep-ph.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{a\gamma}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

hep-ph.title: Generating the Dark Matter mass from the QCD vacuum: A new approach to the mass aspect of the Dark Matter-Baryon coincidence problem
hep-ph.author: Yi Chung
hep-ph.abstract: The comparable abundances of dark matter and baryons imply a deep connection between the dark sector and the QCD sector. In asymmetric dark matter models, the number densities of both sectors are ensured to be similar. However, a complete solution should also include a mechanism relating their masses. In this study, we explore a new mechanism where an $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$ dark matter mass arises from the QCD vacuum. The idea is realized by a strongly coupled chiral dark sector, featuring a light composite fermion as the dark matter. Its mass is generated through the vacuum misalignment induced by QCD, ensuring the mass to be comparable with baryons. The model also features additional light bosons, including GeV-scale dark pions and a composite QCD axion.

hep-ph.title: Space-time Areas and Hadronization Studies
hep-ph.author: S. Abachi, C. Buchanan
hep-ph.abstract: Space-time area laws play a fundamental role in modeling strongly interacting phenomena, such as in relativistic string models, QCD on the lattice, and in hadronization modeling. For the latter, an exact expression for relevant space-time areas related to the final state hadronic events for hadrons of any mass is calculated. Usage of this expression in the UCLA hadronization model helps validate its space-time area law (STAL) principle and unifies the treatment of heavy and light hadrons via a single fragmentation function.

hep-ph.title: Reevaluating the $a_1(1420)$ enhancement and its molecular partners in the low-lying axial-vector meson spectrum
hep-ph.author: Mao-Jun Yan, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate possible axial-vector poles associated with the near-threshold $K^{\ast}\bar K$ interaction, driven by the Weinberg-Tomozawa term and unitarized through the Bethe-Salpeter equation. In the isovector sectors with $I^G(J^{PC})=1^\pm(1^{+\mp})$, we find second-sheet poles below the $K^{\ast}\bar K$ threshold and examine their possible manifestations in the $a_1(1420)$ structure and its possible partner $b_1(1400)$. The corresponding $f_0(980)\pi$ and $\phi\pi$ invariant-mass distributions are compared with the COMPASS and BESIII data, respectively. Within the present framework, the enhancements around 1.4 GeV may be qualitatively understood through the interplay between the triangle-singularity mechanism and the pole-enhanced $K^\ast\bar K$ final-state interaction, although a quantitative description requires a more complete treatment of coupled channels and production dynamics.

hep-ph.title: New Type of Monopoles in QCD and Standard Model
hep-ph.author: Liping Zou, Pengming Zhang, Y. M. Cho
hep-ph.abstract: We present the new monopole solutions in QCD, the Georgi-Glashow model, and the standard model. QCD has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the chromon dressing. The Georgi-Glashow model has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the W boson dressing, in addition to the well-known 'tHooft-Polyakov monopole. Moreover, the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type monopoles which carry the magnetic charge $4\pi/e$ and the electromagnetically neutral type of magnetic monopoles (the naked one and the one with the W boson dressing) which carry the neutral magnetic charge $4\pi/\bae$, where $\bae$ is the neutral charge. We show how to construct the new monopole solutions and clarify the topological origin of the new monopoles. The new monopoles could have deep implications not just in high energy physics but also in condensed matter physics.

hep-ph.title: Heavy Neutrinos across the Electroweak-to-Multi-TeV Frontier via Novel ML-Enhanced Probes
hep-ph.author: Yin-Fa Shen, Alfredo Gurrola, Francesco Romeo, Denis Rathjens, Andres Flórez
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a new strategy to probe heavy neutrinos with non-universal fermion couplings at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) using a novel production mechanism and machine-learning algorithms. Focusing on proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6~\mathrm{TeV}$, we investigate final states containing a charged lepton, missing transverse energy, and two jets. For heavy neutrino masses below $\mathcal{O}(1~\mathrm{TeV})$, production is dominated by the $s$ channel process. At higher masses, vector boson fusion becomes the dominant production mechanism, with cross sections that decrease slowly as the heavy neutrino mass increases. We simulate both signal and Standard Model background events and employ gradient-boosted decision trees to optimize event classification. Assuming an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb^{-1}}$, expected for the high-luminosity, and considering realistic statistical and systematic uncertainties, we find that heavy neutrinos in the mass range $50~\mathrm{GeV}$--$10~\mathrm{TeV}$ can be probed with sensitivity to the mixing parameter $|V_{\ell N}|^2$ spanning from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ to 1. This approach enhances the discovery potential for heavy neutrinos and provides a complementary pathway to existing search strategies.

hep-ph.title: Fluctuation-Induced Backreaction on Bubble-Wall Dynamics in Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions
hep-ph.author: Dongdong Wei, Zong-Kuan Guo
hep-ph.abstract: We study bubble-wall dynamics in cosmological first-order phase transitions in a two-scalar-field model, where the wall is formed by the scalar field $\phi$ and an additional real scalar field $s$ is coupled to it through a portal interaction. We evolve the coupled classical field equations on the lattice and consider a prescribed classical stochastic background of $s$ fluctuations at the onset of the phase transition. Through the portal interaction, this patchy background intermittently modulates the local driving pressure on the wall. The wall consequently undergoes alternating episodes of acceleration and deceleration, with a smaller finite-time averaged propagation rate than in the decoupled limit. A wall-frame analysis of the dynamical $s$-sector energy reveals a coupling-dependent crossover from excess energy deposited behind the wall at weak coupling to a front-side bias at strong coupling. These results demonstrate an additional scalar-field source of bubble-wall backreaction and may affect gravitational-wave and baryogenesis predictions.

hep-ph.title: MadNIS at NLO
hep-ph.author: Giovanni De Crescenzo, Javier Mariño Villadamigo, Nina Elmer, Theo Heimel, Tilman Plehn, Ramon Winterhalder, Marco Zaro
hep-ph.abstract: We combine fast amplitude surrogates with neural importance sampling to accelerate NLO calculations. For virtual corrections, a learned ratio to the Born matrix element with calibrated uncertainties guarantees reliable precision across phase space. For real emission, we stick to the standard FKS subtraction and train sector-conditioned surrogates of the regularized integrands away from divergences. MadNIS then uses multi-channel mappings and FKS sectors as conditions. We validate our approach for electron-positron scattering to three and four jets and find significant speed-ups and variance reduction in the integration.

hep-ph.title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$-symmetric Point
hep-ph.author: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate the dimension-six $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme with perturbative short flow-time expansion coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to $\tau(D_s)/\tau(D^0)$ at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$ symmetric point, we obtain $B_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$,$B_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(70)$, $\epsilon_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$ using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path towards higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.

hep-ph.title: Squeezed double-$b$ tagging for light hadronic resonances at the LHC
hep-ph.author: Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Biswarup Mukhopadhyaya, Sirshendu Samanta, Ritesh K. Singh
hep-ph.abstract: A boosted light resonance decaying into $b\bar b$ can produce a single jet containing two bottom-hadron decay systems. We investigate this squeezed double-$b$ topology using a tracking-based boosted decision tree that distinguishes non-bottom, single-bottom and double-bottom jets. The classifier combines displaced-track multiplicities and momentum fractions with ordered impact parameters and jet kinematics. For the simulated jet samples, the double-bottom tagging response is approximately $83\%$, with corresponding single-bottom and non-bottom mistag responses of $9.7\%$ and $0.5\%$; charm contamination is assessed separately. The tagger is combined with soft-drop mass reconstruction and an event-level classifier using the candidate and recoil jets to identify light hadronic resonances within the QCD background. As an illustrative example, we consider a singlet extension of the flipped two-Higgs-doublet model with pseudoscalar masses of 30, 50 and 60 GeV. The signal samples use a simplified effective-vertex approximation, replacing the momentum-dependent quark-loop production interaction by a local vertex. A resolved loop calculation and higher-order production corrections are beyond the scope of this tagging study. The resulting reconstruction strategy can be applied to different signal hypotheses with their corresponding kinematic acceptance and tagging response.

hep-ph.title: Heavy Quark Transport is Non-Gaussian Beyond Leading Log
hep-ph.author: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld
hep-ph.abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has asymmetric exponential tails that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.

hep-ph.title: Collisional energy loss distribution of a fast parton in a hot or dense QCD medium
hep-ph.author: G. Jackson, S. Peigné
hep-ph.abstract: We compute the probability distribution for collisional energy loss of an ultrarelativistic parton crossing a quark-gluon plasma. This collisional quenching weight has not been determined previously, unlike the average collisional loss per unit distance, although it should be a more accurate quantity to use in jet-quenching phenomenology. The quenching weight is obtained from a well-known kinetic equation which resums an arbitrary number of elastic scatterings of the energetic parton with the medium, providing a complete description of the stochastic energy exchange, including the possibility of energy gain from thermal fluctuations. The formulation also naturally extends the standard treatment of collisional energy loss to finite path lengths, which could be relevant not only for heavy-ion collisions, but also for light-ion, and possibly proton-nucleus and proton-proton collisions. We predict the quenching weight in a setup where individual elastic scatterings are described using the hard thermal loop approximation for soft exchanges, with a smooth matching to the hard domain.

hep-ph.title: Particle species dependence of femtoscopic source parameters in high-energy nuclear collisions
hep-ph.author: Dániel Kincses, László Kovács, Máté Csanád
hep-ph.abstract: High-energy nuclear physics explores the properties of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic collisions of nuclei. Femtoscopy, a subfield of high-energy physics, utilizes quantum-statistical correlations of particles to characterize the space-time geometry of the particle-emitting source. Recent measurements and phenomenological investigations indicated that the shape of the source for identical pions can be well-described by Lévy-stable distributions. The significant power-law tail of the pion source observed both in experiment and in simulations has been shown to originate from the process of Lévy walk during the hadronic scattering phase of the collisions. To better understand the physical processes behind the formation of such power laws, an important next step is to investigate particle species dependence, especially the source shape of identical kaon and proton pairs. As a direct continuation of our previous studies, in this Letter, we present a detailed three-dimensional investigation of the two-particle source shape in simulations of Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV per nucleon pair collision energy using the EPOS3 model. We show the dependence of the extracted femtoscopic source parameters on particle species, centrality and average transverse mass. We find that the scale parameters do not show a clear transverse mass scaling between particle species, as there are systematic differences in the overlapping regions. The power-law exponents of pion and kaon pairs are compatible, while for protons it is higher, closer to the Gaussian limit. When new experimental measurements of kaon and proton correlations become available, these results will provide the basis of a data-model comparison.

hep-ph.title: Critique of Breit-Wigner resonance scattering
hep-ph.author: Philip D. Mannheim
hep-ph.abstract: In the Breit-Wigner approach to scattering the phase shift $\delta$ is to have a form $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ at any real energy continuum scattering resonance. By analytic continuation this leads to complex energy poles in the scattering amplitude at $E_{\rm BW}=E_1-i\Gamma_1$, poles that are identified with unstable physical particles. By solving the square well scattering problem we identify some challenges to this approach. We find that setting $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ is not always a good description of the real energy continuum scattering amplitude, that $\Gamma_1$ can be negative, that $E_{\rm BW}$ is not in fact an energy eigenvalue, and thus cannot be identified with a physical particle. To address these issues we solve the square well Schrödinger problem and find explicit complex energy eigenvalues of the form $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ due to the antilinear $PT$ (Parity, Time Reversal) symmetry of the Hamiltonian. However, $E_2\neq E_1$ and $\Gamma_2\neq \Gamma_1$. As Hamiltonian eigenstates with energy $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ these states can be identified with physical particles and correspond to phase shifts of the form $\tan\delta_{PT} =\Gamma_2/(E_2-E)$. Then by analytic continuation to real energy they give the same real energy resonance shape as a standard Breit-Wigner. However, the determined positions and widths of these resonances should be associated with $E_2$ and $\Gamma_2$ rather than with $E_1$ and $\Gamma_1$. We thus recognize two forms of resonance in the real energy scattering amplitude $f(E)$, those associated with the continuum (the complex $E$ plane branch cut) and those due to poles in the complex $E$ plane. Only the latter can be associated with real particles. The continuum resonances are not associated with Breit-Wigner modes, and the number of such resonances correlates with the number of square well bound states.

hep-ph.title: B Meson Semi-Invisible Decays via Perturbative QCD
hep-ph.author: Han-Bing Liu, Ye Xing, Bin Luo
hep-ph.abstract: This paper focuses on the dark sector decay processes of $B$ mesons ($B\to \mathcal{B}_8\ +$ invisible). Using the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach, we calculate the upper bounds on the branching ratios for decays from $B$ mesons into light baryons and dark baryons within two distinct $B$-Mesogenesis scenarios. A detailed discussion of the form factor $B\to \mathcal{B}_8$ is presented. Based on the derived form factors and effective couplings, we then reach the final numerical analysis. The results show that these upper bounds can reach sizable, especially for $B^0\to n\psi$ in Type-I scenario, with values of orderis $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ . Such processes are expected to facilitate the search for dark matter at hadron colliders and B factories.

hep-ph.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
hep-ph.author: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu
hep-ph.abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

hep-ph.title: Phenomenology of heavy-flavour jet angularities at hadron colliders
hep-ph.author: Andrea Ghira, Lorenzo Mai, Simone Marzani, Daniel Reichelt, Steffen Schumann, Leon Stöcker
hep-ph.abstract: We compute resummed and matched predictions for jet angularities in hadronic Z+jet events, where the jet is initiated by a b-quark. The analysis is performed both with and without grooming the candidate jets using the SoftDrop algorithm. Mass effects are consistently included at both fixed-order and resummed levels. Our theoretical predictions also incorporate non-perturbative corrections from the underlying event and hadronization, implemented through parton-to-hadron transfer matrices extracted from dedicated Monte Carlo simulations with Sherpa. Finally, we compare results for b-jets with the ones from light-flavour jets, in order to quantify the impact of finite-mass effects.

hep-ph.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
hep-ph.author: Ch. M. Benavides, C. S. Muñoz, B. C. Canas, Eduardo Rojas
hep-ph.abstract: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_\mu$ and $L_e-L_\tau$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.

hep-ph.title: Neutron tagging of heavy lepton pair production at RHIC and LHC energies
hep-ph.author: Atacan Fatih Candar, Mehmet Cem Güçlü
hep-ph.abstract: We calculated cross sections for $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow \ell^+\ell^-$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) production in ultraperipheral gold and lead collisions and compare our results with recent measurements from the STAR, ALICE, ATLAS, and CMS experiments at center of mass energies $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76 $ TeV, and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. The calculations are performed within lowest order quantum electrodynamics (LO QED) using a Monte Carlo technique for calculating the impact parameter dependent probability, and subsequently combined with neutron emission probabilities associated with Coulomb excitation of the nuclei. These neutron emission scenarios are modeled using a Poisson statistics, allowing the cross sections to be categorized into experimentally relevant neutron classes: 0n0n, 0nXn, XnXn, and inclusive (0n0n+0nXn+XnXn) production. To enable a direct comparison with experiments, fiducial phase space restrictions corresponding to the acceptance of each detector are implemented.

hep-ph.title: Beyond leading-logarithm photon production from two-loop diagrams in a hot QCD medium
hep-ph.author: Sumit, Ritesh Ghosh, Munshi G. Mustafa
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate high-energy photon production from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes in a quark-gluon plasma by evaluating the imaginary part of the two-loop photon self-energies in thermal QCD. Working in the imaginary-time formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the leading-logarithmic and beyond-leading-logarithmic contributions to the photon production rate from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. We retain the full Fermi--Dirac and Bose--Einstein statistical factors and compare the resulting Compton and annihilation rates with those obtained from kinetic theory and the closed-time-path formalism. The summed rates agree with the corresponding established results, providing a nontrivial consistency check of the calculation. Furthermore, when we consider the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution for incoming particles, we find that quantum corrections are absent in the individual $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. However, the total rate agrees with that of full statistics.

hep-ph.title: Dynamical flattening of halo density cusps by Q-ball dark matter
hep-ph.author: Alexander Libanov, Sergey Troitsky
hep-ph.abstract: Cold, collisionless dark matter successfully explains a wide range of observations, including the formation of large-scale structure. Nevertheless, tensions remain on small, galactic scales, most notably the cusp-core, or inner-mass-deficit, problem and the diversity of inner rotation-curve shapes and central densities at fixed halo mass. These observations suggest that additional dark-sector physics may affect the inner structure of halos, although no generally accepted explanation has yet emerged. Here, making use of a toy but representative model, we investigate how interacting dark-matter Q-balls -- non-topological solitons stabilized by a conserved charge -- modify halo centers and generate a diversity of inner profiles. Our calculations include merger-induced mass and kinetic-energy losses, elastic heat transport, and the gravitational readjustment of the halo; flattening and later recontraction can both occur. Produced in the early Universe in the dark sector, these Q-balls grow in the dense central regions of halos, while their interaction cross section decreases as the soliton mass increases. This process operates preferentially in halo centers, converting part of the rest-mass energy stored in massive Q-balls into relativistic dark-sector particles and thereby modifying the inner mass-density profile. The resulting density-dependent energy loss competes with heat transport and halo response. An ensemble of initial assembly conditions yields very different final densities at fixed microphysics, although neither a universal constant-density core nor a statistical fit to the observed population is established.

hep-ph.title: Heavy neutral leptons beyond the BBN bound: probing the lepton asymmetry of the Universe
hep-ph.author: Kensuke Akita, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Vsevolod Syvolap
hep-ph.abstract: Hadronically decaying particles with lifetimes $\tau\gtrsim0.02\,{\rm s}$ are excluded by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis almost independently of their abundance: the mesons from their decays convert protons into neutrons faster than the reverse, and helium is overproduced. For heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), this blankets the couplings the upcoming accelerator searches can reach. We propose a scenario with large lepton flavor asymmetries in which HNLs evade it. A Dirac HNL decays into $\pi^+$ and its antiparticle into $\pi^-$, so an asymmetry between the two populations injects an excess of $\pi^+$, which converts the neutrons back to their standard abundance, while a cancellation between the asymmetries and the HNL decays keeps the shift in $N_{\rm eff}$ small. This opens the parameter space with $m_l+m_\pi\lesssim m_N\lesssim1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $\tau_N\lesssim1\,{\rm s}$, including a substantial region within the reach of SHiP. A discovery there, combined with the BBN and CMB observables, would fix the primordial flavor asymmetries up to one remaining direction. The relic neutrino background and gravitational waves from the QCD transition epoch may probe that direction, and with it the lepton asymmetry of the Universe.

hep-ph.title: Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin $B$-Meson Decays
hep-ph.author: Yong-Kang Huang, Yu-Ming Wang, Xue-Chen Zhao
hep-ph.abstract: We compute for the first time the subleading twist correction to the exclusive rare $b \to \left \{s, d \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays from the three-particle $B$-meson distribution amplitude at next-to-leading order accuracy by employing the soft-collinear effective theory. This constitutes the last missing ingredient for the complete factorization analysis of the hadronic matrix element of the weak effective Hamiltonian at leading power in the heavy quark expansion. Incorporating further a variety of the next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the spectator-scattering amplitude and the weak annihilation topology, we then present the improved field-theoretic predictions for phenomenologically interesting observables in the electroweak penguin $B \to \left \{K, \pi \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays.

hep-ph.title: Mixing-angle sensitivity of inclusive $Ξ_{bc} $ and $Ω_{bc}$ lifetimes
hep-ph.author: Hai-Yang Cheng, Chia-Wei Liu, Fanrong Xu
hep-ph.abstract: We study the inclusive lifetimes of $\Xi_{bc}^{+}$, $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$, and $\Omega_{bc}^{0}$ with emphasis on the mixing between the spin-zero and spin-one $bc$-diquark configurations. The matrix elements are evaluated in both the homogeneous bag model (HBM) and the nonrelativistic quark model (NRQM). At the benchmark mixing angles $-23.0^\circ$ for $\Xi_{bc}$ and $-23.5^\circ$ for $\Omega_{bc}$, the corresponding lifetime triplets are $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.421^{+0.098}_{-0.093}{}^{+0.007}_{-0.014},0.075^{+0.035}_{-0.017}{}^{+0.004}_{-0.001},0.223^{+0.074}_{-0.046}{}^{+0.018}_{-0.012})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in HBM and $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.367^{+0.076}_{-0.070}{}^{+0.001}_{-0.005},0.100^{+0.032}_{-0.014}{}^{+0.006}_{-0.001},0.229^{+0.066}_{-0.042}{}^{+0.017}_{-0.011})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in NRQM. The first errors are the fixed-angle uncertainties; the second are the envelopes from varying each mixing angle by $\pm10^\circ$ with all other inputs fixed. Relative to the unmixed spin-one reference points, the $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$ and $\Omega_{bc}$ lifetimes decrease by approximately $17\%$-$19\%$. Neither the minimum nor the maximum of the central lifetime curves occurs at a pure $S_{bc}=0$ or $S_{bc}=1$ configuration; the extrema instead lie at mixed angles with $|\phi_{\cal B}|\simeq27^\circ$-$63^\circ$. The two pure-spin cases alone are therefore insufficient to characterize the angular dependence.

hep-ph.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
hep-ph.author: Alex Prygarin, Claudelle Capasia Madjuogang Sandeu, Karam Shekh Yusuf
hep-ph.abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.

hep-ph.title: Sub-MeV gamma-ray lines from an endothermic interpretation of the LZ recoil candidate
hep-ph.author: Maíra Dutra, Jacinto P. Neto, Clarissa Siqueira
hep-ph.abstract: Endothermic upscattering of heavy dark matter offers a compelling interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil candidate recently reported by LUX-ZEPLIN, with a characteristic recoil energy $E_R \propto \delta$, where $\delta$ is the mass splitting between the dark matter states. Cosmological and experimental constraints motivate the depletion of the primordial heavier state, which can be regenerated in the Galactic halo. We show that, if the heavier state decays radiatively, the same mass splitting sets the energy of a gamma-ray line, $E_\gamma \simeq \delta$. For our benchmark, this leads to a sub-MeV line within the projected reach of the Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), scheduled for launch in 2027. The confirmation of the LUX-ZEPLIN candidate event as a dark matter signal would therefore motivate dedicated searches for sub-MeV gamma-ray lines, with COSI providing a timely opportunity to test this interpretation.

hep-ph.title: M1 Radiative Transitions in the $B_c$ System after the $B_c^\ast(1S)$ Observation: Radial-Node Cancellation and Quark-Line Filtering
hep-ph.author: Bing-Dong Wan
hep-ph.abstract: The recent ATLAS observation of the $B_c^*(1S)$ meson fixes the photon momentum for $B_c^*(1S)\to B_c(1S)\gamma$. We calculate four $1S$ and $2S$ M1 radiative transitions with relativistic Salpeter wave functions calibrated to the measured ground-state masses, and obtain $\Gamma[B_c^*(1S)\to B_c(1S)\gamma]=5.24\times10^{-2}$~keV. For the hindered $2S\to1S$ transitions, contributions from different radial-momentum regions largely cancel, leaving form factors about 25 times smaller than that of the ground-state allowed transition. The cancellation factors, defined as the ratio of the integral of the absolute radial contribution to the magnitude of the net integral, are approximately 18--20. Nevertheless, the hindered radiative widths are not suppressed, because their much larger photon momenta compensate for the smaller form factors. Separating the photon-emission contributions of the $b$ quark and $\bar c$ antiquark, we find particularly strong cancellation in the $b$ contribution to $B_c(2S)\to B_c^*(1S)\gamma$: only about $0.46\%$ of the integrated absolute radial contribution remains after cancellation, compared with about $4.5\%$ for the $\bar c$ contribution. The unmeasured $B_c^*(2S)$ mass remains the main limitation on the $2S\to2S$ radiative width.

hep-ph.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
hep-ph.author: Giorgio Galanti
hep-ph.abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

hep-ph.title: A Chiral Nelson-Barr Relaxion
hep-ph.author: Cristien Arzate, Joshua Iascau
hep-ph.abstract: We present the chiral Nelson-Barr relaxion model, an extension of the Nelson-Barr relaxion framework with a gauged chiral $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. It includes vector-like quarks to cancel gauge anomalies and a scalar whose vacuum expectation value generates their masses. The chiral symmetry forbids the leading operators responsible for the Nelson-Barr and clockwork quality problems. Right-handed neutrinos generate light-neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism and permit thermal leptogenesis. For the particular Nelson-Barr sector Yukawa coupling considered, relaxion phenomenology gives a maximal scale of $CP$ violation $f_{\textrm{max}}^{\textrm{pheno}}\sim 4 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV}$, about an order of magnitude greater than the corresponding phenomenological ceiling in the original model. The model can accommodate thermal leptogenesis if its right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating history satisfy the Davidson-Ibarra bound.

hep-ph.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
hep-ph.author: Chris D. White
hep-ph.abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

hep-ph.title: Magnetars magnetic field evolution with ambipolar diffusion
hep-ph.author: Monika Sinha, Manoj Kumar Ghosh, Yogeesh N
hep-ph.abstract: The magnetic field associated with neutron stars is generally believed to be threaded inside the star. In the presence of a magnetic field, plasma in the interior of the star undergoes a series of processes that result in magnetic field evolution. It is believed that magnetar activities like X-ray, gamma-ray bursts, and giant flares (which release more energy in a few sec than Sun in 10 years), are mainly due to field decay. The most important process of field decay inside the core of the star is the ambipolar diffusion of the charged particles present in the interior plasma. The decay rate due to ambipolar diffusion is directly connected to the ambipolar velocity of the charged particles under the influence of the present magnetic field. The ambipolar velocity of the charged particles depends on the internal dynamics of the particles. We outline a general method to solve the particle dynamics in the presence of a magnetic field to have a magnetohydrodynamics equation from ambipolar velocity. The equation is general and applicable to all possible surrounding conditions temperature, matter states like normal or superfluid, etc.

hep-ph.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization
hep-ph.author: Luca Caloni, Serena Giardiello, Margherita Lembo, Martina Gerbino, Giulia Gubitosi, Massimiliano Lattanzi, Luca Pagano
hep-ph.abstract: We perform a comprehensive study of the signatures of Lorentz violation in electrodynamics on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropies. In the framework of the minimal Standard Model Extension (SME), we consider effects generated by renormalizable operators, both CPT-odd and CPT-even. These operators are responsible for sourcing, respectively, cosmic birefringence and circular polarization. We propagate jointly the effects of all the relevant Lorentz-violating parameters to CMB observables and provide constraints with the most recent CMB datasets. We bound the CPT-even coefficient to $k_{F,E+B} < 6.02 \times 10^{-32}$ at 95\% CL. This improves previous CMB bounds by more than one order of magnitude. The limits we obtain on the CPT-odd coefficients, i.e. $|k_{(V)00}^{(3)}| < 1.05 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}| < 0.51 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ at 95\% CL, are respectively one and two orders of magnitude stronger than previous CMB-based limits, superseding also bounds from non-CMB searches. This analysis provides the strongest constraints to date on CPT-violating coefficients in the minimal SME from CMB searches.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational Waves from Collisions of Fuzzy Dark Matter Solitons
hep-ph.author: Chen Tan, Jing-Kang Bin, Ke Wang
hep-ph.abstract: According to the Schrödinger-Poisson (SP) equations, fuzzy dark matter (FDM) can form a stable equilibrium configuration, the so-called FDM soliton. The SP system can also determine the evolution of FDM solitons, such as head-on collision. In this paper, we first propose a new adimensional unit of length, time and mass. And then, we simulate the adimensional SP system with $\mathtt{PyUltraLight}$ to study the GWs from collision of FDM solitons when the linearized theory is valid and the GW back reaction on the evolution of FDM solitons is ignored. Finally, we find that the GWs from collisions have a frequency of (few ten-years)$^{-1}$ or (few years)$^{-1}$ when FDM mass is $m=10^{-18}\rm{eV}/c^2$ or $m=10^{-17}\rm{eV}/c^2$. Therefore, future detection of such GWs will constrain the property of FDM particle and solitons.

hep-ph.title: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
hep-ph.author: Laura Iacconi, David Mulryne, David Seery
hep-ph.abstract: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $\delta N$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $\delta N$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.

hep-ph.title: Amplifying the Cosmological Collider with Ghost Spectators
hep-ph.author: Matheus C. Ferreira, Felipe T. Falciano, Guilherme L. Pimentel
hep-ph.abstract: Ghost inflation is a well-known framework in which cosmological fluctuations can generate enhanced primordial non-Gaussianity, typically of the equilateral type. In its original form, however, it is in tension with current observational constraints. Here we instead consider a setup in which a standard inflaton drives the background evolution, while excitations of a ghost condensate act as spectator fields that interact with the inflaton. This proposal fits naturally within the cosmological collider program: the exchanged particle has a modified dispersion relation, $\omega \propto k^2$. We show that this ghost-inspired dynamics weakens the usual Boltzmann suppression, similarly to models with a very small effective sound speed, yielding an enhanced bispectrum signal relative to standard cosmological collider scenarios. At the same time, the horizon-crossing scale remains a free parameter of the theory. As a result, the model shares features of both the de Sitter bootstrap and boostless frameworks. Finally, we derive the differential equations governing cosmological correlators in the ghost-collider setup. Their structure reflects the quadratic momentum dependence of the dispersion relation and distinguishes this scenario from conventional relativistic cases.

hep-ph.title: Heavy-Meson Bag Parameters using Gradient Flow
hep-ph.author: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel
hep-ph.abstract: We demonstrate the use of the gradient flow combined with the short flow-time expansion (GF+SFTX) as a renormalization procedure for four-quark operator matrix elements and associated bag parameters relevant to neutral heavy-meson mixing ($\Delta Q=2$) and heavy-meson lifetimes ($\Delta Q=0$). Using six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we calculate for a charm-strange system with physical quark masses flowed bag parameters and match them to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme using perturbative SFTX coefficients up to next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD. We employ a multiscale matching strategy and a renormalization-group improved flow-time evolution which allows for a reliable estimate of systematic uncertainties. For a fictitious neutral $D_s$ meson, we obtain the $\Delta Q=2$ $\overline{\text{MS}}$ bag parameter ${\cal B}^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.7673(123)$, consistent with existing short-distance $D^0$ mixing determinations. For the $\Delta Q=0$ lifetime-ratio operator basis, we find the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ results $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$, $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(71)$, $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$. We provide conversion formulae to re-express these results for an arbitrary choice of evanescent operators. These results demonstrate that GF+SFTX can deliver precise determinations of dimension-six four-quark operators and establish a framework for future lattice computations including more complex operator bases, where the challenge of power-divergent mixing is shifted to the continuum and handled in the SFTX.

hep-ph.title: All-order structure of static gravitational interactions and the seventh post-Newtonian potential
hep-ph.author: Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Sid Smith, Jan Steinhoff
hep-ph.abstract: We present a closed formula for the computation of static post-Newtonian corrections to the two-body gravitational dynamics at any odd order, assuming the lower-order results are known. The formula is derived within a correlation function framework and exploits the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry of the static sector, leading to a novel theoretical interpretation of the factorization theorem. As an application, we compute the gravitational interaction of two compact coalescing objects at the seventh post-Newtonian order in the static limit, which receives contributions from seven-loop graphs at order $\mathcal{O}(G_N^8 v^0)$, and find complete agreement with the results obtained using the diagrammatic approach of the factorization theorem.

hep-ph.title: Sequential Bayesian inference with correlated heavy-ion datasets
hep-ph.author: Lipei Du
