hep-ph.abstract: Bayesian inference provides a natural framework for updating knowledge as new information becomes available, often in a sequential manner by incorporating datasets in stages or reusing previous posteriors as priors. A common implementation uses a factorized update in which datasets are treated as conditionally independent. When datasets have statistically correlated uncertainties, however, this approximation generally becomes inconsistent with the joint likelihood and can lead to distorted posterior constraints. In this work, we investigate this issue in a controlled setting using pseudo-data with a tunable covariance structure. We compare joint inference, factorized sequential updating, and a formulation based on the exact conditional likelihood. We show that factorized updates reproduce the joint posterior under conditional independence, but develop systematic deviations when correlations are neglected, with discrepancies that increase with correlation strength in our numerical examples. In contrast, conditional sequential updating reproduces the joint posterior exactly. To interpret these deviations, we introduce an information decomposition that separates the joint information into contributions from the first dataset and the conditional information provided by the second. By comparing marginal and conditional information, we show that correlations induce structured changes in the constraints on different parameter combinations, reflecting the interplay between covariance structure and dataset sensitivities. This information-based analysis provides a quantitative interpretation of the observed posterior discrepancies. These results provide a practical diagnostic for assessing the consistency of sequential Bayesian inference with correlated datasets and highlight the need for a consistent treatment of correlations within a common probabilistic framework.

hep-ph.title: Higher Mellin Moments of the Unpolarized PDF of the Pion and the Kaon from Lattice QCD
hep-ph.author: Constantia Alexandrou(Univ. of Cyprus and The Cyprus Inst.), Simone Bacchio(The Cyprus Inst.), Priyajit Jana(Univ. of Cyprus and The Cyprus Inst.), Marcus Petschlies(Univ. of Bonn), Luis Alberto Rodriguez Chacon(The Cyprus Inst. and Univ. of Ferrara), Gregoris Spanoudes(Univ. of Cyprus), Fernanda Steffens(Univ. of Bonn), Carsten Urbach(Univ. of Bonn), Urs Wenger(Univ. of Bern)
hep-ph.abstract: We present results on the Mellin moments of the unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) of the pion and kaon up to the fourth order. The computation is done using one $N_f=2+1+1$ gauge ensemble of twisted mass fermions with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical values. We reconstruct the valence pion and kaon PDFs using the connected contributions to the three Mellin moments. We compare our results on the Mellin moments and the reconstructed PDFs with other lattice QCD and phenomenological determinations.

hep-ph.title: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
hep-ph.author: Satyabrata Datta, Rome Samanta
hep-ph.abstract: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssim\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.

hep-ph.title: Dressed Fock Spaces in Gauge Theory and Gravity
hep-ph.author: Sangmin Choi, Prahar Mitra
hep-ph.abstract: Four-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories exhibit long-range interactions that require asymptotic particles to be dressed by clouds of soft photons and gravitons. Faddeev-Kulish dressings render scattering amplitudes infrared-finite, but the resulting multi-particle states do not factorise into tensor products of dressed one-particle states. We show that this loss of Fock-space factorisation is not fundamental, but reflects an inappropriate choice of infrared variables. The real soft divergence is reproduced by the Goldstone modes of asymptotic symmetries, while the Coulomb phase is reproduced by new zero modes of the radiative fields that we introduce here. In these variables, infrared-finite dressed multi-particle states admit the usual Fock-space factorisation into single-particle dressed states.

hep-ph.title: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
hep-ph.author: Han Lai, Atsuhisa Ota
hep-ph.abstract: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_\tau h_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.

hep-ph.title: Cooling, conduction, and compact objects: Gravothermal evolution of dissipative self-interacting dark matter halos
hep-ph.author: Ludwig D. Schmidt, Moritz S. Fischer, Mathias Garny
hep-ph.abstract: Many proposed self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models yield radiative processes that can dissipate energy. Understanding their impact on astrophysical objects through simulations and comparing the results with observations may thus constrain SIDM models. We systematically investigated how dissipation alters the gravothermal evolution of isolated SIDM halos by independently varying dissipation and heat conduction and identified potential observational signatures. We present the first extension of the $N$-body formalism for frequent small-angle self-interactions to include effective dissipation. We compared all results for isolated halos with a dissipative gravothermal fluid model to assess the validity and limitations of the latter. We find that dissipation qualitatively changes the gravothermal evolution of SIDM halos beyond simply accelerating collapse. Sufficiently strong central cooling can invert the usual role of heat conduction: the formation of an isothermal core is suppressed such that conduction remains directed inward throughout the evolution. Outer halo regions beyond the scale radius can cool efficiently rather than being heated by conduction, resulting in a larger region of mass infall and a less pronounced indentation between the core and the outer halo in the final density profile. These effects depend strongly on the cooling rate but are comparatively insensitive to the angular dependence of the self-interaction cross section. We further show that weakly dissipative self-interactions can explain the properties of the recently observed strong lens perturber in JVAS B1938+666 with significantly shorter evolution times or, equivalently, smaller cross sections compared to the elastic case. Our results open a new route to connecting halo structure and recently reported compact objects to dark-sector microphysics.

hep-ph.title: Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge
hep-ph.author: Xiaojun Yao
hep-ph.abstract: We study quantum simulation of SU(3) non-Abelian gauge theory dynamically coupled with fundamental fermions in $3+1$ dimensions by employing the lattice Hamiltonian in axial gauge under fixed boundary conditions, which avoids Gauss's law constraints. The temporal component of the gauge field is analytically solved in terms of independent field degrees of freedom and a lattice regulated Green's function. The axial gauge condition is trivially maintained in time evolution, even under Trotterization. The gauge field degrees of freedom are expressed in the local field basis and can be efficiently transformed into the canonical conjugate momentum basis by local quantum Fourier transforms. We prove the number of qubits needed for describing all states up to an energy $E$ with an accuracy $\epsilon$ on a lattice of volume $V$ at bare coupling $g$ is bounded as $16n_A V + 12n_f V$, where $n_A \approx \log_2 (\frac{64 E' V^{4/3}}{\pi^2\epsilon} + \frac{32\sqrt{2}g n_f E'^{1/2} V^{7/6}}{\sqrt{3}\pi^3\epsilon^{1/2}} ) $ is the number of qubits needed for each independent gauge field per site with a shifted energy $E'$, and $n_f$ denotes the number of fermion flavors. We then analyze a quantum algorithm for time evolution that is based on Trotterization, quantum Fourier transform, and Jordan-Wigner transformation, for which quantum circuits can be explicitly constructed under arbitrary gauge field truncation and digitization. We find the numbers of CNOT and single-qubit rotation gates scale as $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3}) + O(V^{5/3})$ and $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3})$, respectively, per Trotter step for fixed $n_f\leq 6$. Together with the bounded Trotterization error, we conclude that quantum resources needed for simulating real-time dynamics of lattice QCD scale polynomially with volume, energy, time, accuracy, and bare Hamiltonian parameters.

hep-ph.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: Conditions for a Local Type IIB D3-D7-D3 Mechanism of Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
hep-ph.author: Michaël Sarrazin
hep-ph.abstract: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate the conditions under which a local Type IIB D3$_+$-D7-D3$_-$/E3 configuration can generate perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Assuming the required charged zero-mode spectrum, neutral instanton measure and non-vanishing charged disk amplitudes, we derive an E3-induced chiral mass term with scalar and pseudoscalar components. The latter reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. This yields a conditional matching to the two-sheeted operator within the effective field theory. A separate orbifold example checks the charged zero-mode representations and the compensating instanton charge. Whether all the required instanton ingredients coexist with two independent massive D3-D7 matter sectors at separated endpoints in a single local configuration remains open. We outline a model-building roadmap toward such a configuration and its compact phenomenological embedding. Such an embedding requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.

hep-ph.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
hep-ph.author: Bence Szentkuti, Mate Csanad
hep-ph.abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second, a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP), is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that Lévy distributions describe the shape of hadron (pion) emission sources at freeze-out the most accurately; however, based on hydrodynamics Gaussian distributions are typically expected. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing Lévy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations; in particular, the effective temperatures from angle-averaged transverse mass distributions and the femtoscopic radii from two-particle momentum correlation functions are analyzed.

hep-ph.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
hep-ph.author: Xiaolin Wang, Xingyu Guo, Jinyang Li, Tianyin Li, Enke Wang, Lingxiao Wang, Hongxi Xing
hep-ph.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

hep-ph.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
hep-ph.author: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh
hep-ph.abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in Gauss-Bonnet braneworld cosmology
hep-ph.author: Ian B Whittingham
hep-ph.abstract: The present study investigates the feasibility of gravitational baryogenesis in a Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) type II braneworld cosmology. The modified expansion rate of the Universe in this scenario evolves through three distinct expansion regimes, the GB regime at early times where the expansion rate $H \sim \rho^{1/3}$ falls more slowly than the standard expansion law $H\sim \rho^{1/2}$ of GR, then the RS type era with an enhanced expansion $H \sim \rho$, before finally reducing to the standard expansion law in the low energy limit. Gravitational baryogenesis depends on $\dot{R}$ and requires $\dot{R} <0$. This condition is satisfied for the GB and GR regimes. However, $\dot{R}>0$ for the RS regime and successful baryogenesis requires either that the decoupling temperature occurs during the GB regime or that the Universe makes a direct transition from the GB regime to the GR regime.The GB baryon asymmetry $\eta(T)$ is proportional to $\mu (1+w)(1-w)(1+1/\beta)$, where $\mu$ is the energy scale $\mu \equiv 1/l$ associated with the bulk curvature scale $l$, $\beta \equiv 4 \alpha \mu^{2}$, where $\alpha$ is the GB coupling, and $w$ is the equation of state parameter $p=w \rho$. Studies of inflation in GB-braneworld cosmology place constraints on the allowed ranges of the parameters $\mu$ and $\beta$. Guided by these, the asymmetry has been calculated for ranges of $(\mu, \beta, w)$ and it is found that the observed values can be obtained for a value of $\beta$ within the range $(10^{-2} - 10^{-3})$ for $\mu =10^{12}$ GeV, and within the range $(10^{-1}- 10^{-2})$ for $\mu =10^{13}$ GeV. All values of $\eta$ for $\mu=10^{14}$ are too high. The parameter ranges for the decoupling temperatures required to produce the observed asymmetry have also been established.

hep-ph.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
hep-ph.author: Samuel Sánchez López, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno Sánchez
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

hep-ph.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
hep-ph.author: Nicholas Kamp, Louis Deslauriers, Carlos A. Argüelles, Gonzalo Herrera, William G. Thompson
hep-ph.abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

hep-lat.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
hep-lat.author: Alessandro Mariani
hep-lat.abstract: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

hep-lat.title: Critical behavior of the bosonized Schwinger model with uniform matrix product states
hep-lat.author: Takuya Okuda
hep-lat.abstract: Quantum electrodynamics in two spacetime dimensions, also known as the Schwinger model, admits a dual formulation in terms of a non-compact boson field. Using a Hamiltonian lattice discretization of the bosonized model, we compute the critical mass of the continuum Schwinger model at $\theta=\pi$. We numerically obtain the ground state on an infinite chain by the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm, preserving charge conjugation exactly. As a truncated basis for the local Hilbert space, we employ the oscillator basis that diagonalizes the one-site reduced density matrix of the free limit. We constrain the fitting functions for the continuum extrapolation using the Symanzik effective theory for lattice corrections. Our result for the critical mass, $(m/g)_c = 0.333\,555(5)$, agrees with recent staggered-fermion determinations at comparable precision.

hep-lat.title: Automatic O(a) Improvement for Wilson Twisted Mass Fermions in the Hamiltonian Formulation
hep-lat.author: Carsten Urbach
hep-lat.abstract: We apply the recently developed Symanzik effective Hamiltonian framework to Wilson twisted mass fermions. The effective Hamiltonian is constructed solely based on the symmetries of the lattice Hamiltonian without recourse to the Symanzik effective action in Euclidean space-time. We use it to prove automatic $O(a)$ improvement at maximal twist, as well as $O(a)$ improvement via so-called mass and Wilson average. Moreover, we derive the structure of $O(a)$ counterterms pre-requisite for clover on-shell improvement of Wilson fermions. We show how to remove on-shell redundant contributions using canonical transformations, and find that the well known clover term in isotropic Euclidean space time splits into two terms with independent coefficients.

hep-lat.title: Numerical tests of chiral fermion weights with $η$-invariant phases in the 3450 model
hep-lat.author: Tatsuhiro Misumi
hep-lat.abstract: We test numerically a recently proposed prescription for coupling continuum chiral fermions to interpolated lattice gauge fields, in which the fermion weight has a Pauli-Villars (PV) regularized magnitude and a phase given by an Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant in one higher dimension. We use the anomaly-free two-dimensional $U(1)$ theory with left-handed charges $3,4$ and right-handed charges $5,0$, whose torus determinant is known exactly. At zero magnetic flux, with gauge fields interpolated from lattice links, the Polyakov loops evaluated on a $16\times16$ grid of flat connections agree with the exact values within $0.04\%$, whereas omitting the APS phase substantially reduces them to about $3\%$ of the exact result. The vacuum-polarization response yields an induced mass $m/e=2.82089$, close to $5/\sqrt{\pi}=2.82095$. At unit flux, where zero modes make the determinant vanish, we calculate a twelve-point correlator on a cylinder with the generalized APS boundary condition. For three smooth backgrounds its magnitude agrees with the exact result within $0.8\%$. Without the $\eta$-invariant its phase deviates by $1.8$-$3.0$ mrad, and with it by $0.2$-$0.5$ mrad. The phase of each charged fermion changes by $15$-$46$ mrad when the gauge field is extended differently into the third dimension, but the change cancels to below $0.2$ mrad in the anomaly-free combination.

hep-lat.title: $NΩ$ Dibaryon near Unitarity from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Liang Zhang, Yan Lyu, Sinya Aoki, Takumi Doi, Tetsuo Hatsuda, Song Zhang, Yu-Gang Ma
hep-lat.abstract: The $N\Omega$ system is a promising dibaryon candidate because its constituents share no valence quarks and therefore avoid valence-quark Pauli repulsion. We determine the $^{5}S_{2}$ $N\Omega$ interaction in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD at physical quark masses ($m_\pi\simeq137~\text{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method. The interaction is attractive over the resolved range and supports a shallow state near unitarity. A direct $T$-matrix pole analysis gives $B_{n\Omega} = 0.61\,(^{+0.41}_{-0.30})\,(^{+0.60}_{-0.18})~\text{MeV}$; including finite-charge-size Coulomb attraction yields $B_{p\Omega} = 1.25\,(^{+0.46}_{-0.39})\,(^{+0.69}_{-0.25})~\text{MeV}$. These results provide a first-principles benchmark for future $N\Omega$ femtoscopy and dibaryon searches.

hep-lat.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $χ$EFT and lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Md. Emanuel Hoque(Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI), Arunava Mukherjee(Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI), Sayantan Sharma(The Institute of Mathematical Sciences/HBNI)
hep-lat.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

hep-lat.title: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
hep-lat.author: C. Wetterich
hep-lat.abstract: The time evolution of the probability distribution for classical fields can be described by the quantum formalism. For free classical fields the free quantum field theory arises as a subsystem. Different probability distributions for classical fields correspond to the classical thermal equilibrium with the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence or the quantum thermal equilibrium with the Planck spectrum. The selection of the Rayleigh-Jeans or Planck spectrum is not a question of fundamental concepts. It becomes an issue of dynamical selection once interactions are present. We compare the momentum dependence of the classical energy and field correlations for the classical and quantum equilibrium. This permits to decide which equilibrium is selected as a result of asymptotic dynamics by numerical simulations of the probabilistic classical fields including interactions. For free probabilistic classical fields we construct a general ``classical-quantum map'' between the classical probability distribution and the density matrix of the quantum field theory.

hep-lat.title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
hep-lat.author: Narmin Nasibova, Francesco Giacosa
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.

hep-lat.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
hep-lat.author: Zhengwen Liu
hep-lat.abstract: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $\eta$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.

hep-lat.title: Gauge Theory Bootstrap with varying $N_c$
hep-lat.author: Rafael Cordoba, Yifei He, Martin Kruczenski, Derek Ping, Jignesh Mohanty, Emil Alegria
hep-lat.abstract: We use the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study asymptotically free gauge theories with a varying number of colors $N_c$. The parameter $N_c$ enters the computation through the sum rules and asymptotic form factors, allowing us to tune this microscopic parameter directly and examine the corresponding low-energy strongly coupled dynamics. For $3\le N_c\le 12$, we extract the scattering lengths, effective ranges, and low-energy constants $\bar{l}_i$, and study their $N_c$ dependence. We also obtain the $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $f_2$ resonances for the same range of $N_c$. The $\rho$ and $f_2$ masses depend only weakly on $N_c$, and their widths decrease as $N_c$ increases, consistent with the $1/N_c$ scaling expected for conventional $q\bar{q}$ mesons. In contrast, the $\sigma$ meson mass and width both increase with $N_c$, in agreement with a previous unitarized $\chi$PT analysis. These results provide a further test of the Gauge Theory Bootstrap for studying asymptotically free gauge theories.

hep-lat.title: Unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory on a triangular lattice: deconfined fermions in a vison crystal and superfluidity
hep-lat.author: Welberth Kennedy, João C. Inácio, Fakher F. Assaad
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate an unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory coupled to fermions on the triangular lattice at half filling, using auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The triangular geometry gives rise to a global $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry that acts as an Ising symmetry on the plaquette fluxes. At weak transverse field $h$, this symmetry is spontaneously broken, stabilizing a vison crystal. We argue that this phase is deconfined: fermions, charged under an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field, propagate in an ordered $\pi$-flux background and form a Dirac semimetal. Increasing the transverse field triggers a first-order quantum phase transition to a confined $s$-wave superfluid, at which confinement and global symmetry breaking occur simultaneously. This contrasts with the square lattice, where the corresponding transition is continuous. We extend our analysis to finite temperature and determine the thermal phase boundaries of both ordered phases. The superfluid melts through a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, whereas the vison crystal undergoes a thermal Ising transition. Together, our results establish the $T \times h$ phase diagram and demonstrate how the triangular geometry leads to qualitative changes in both the phases and the criticality of the model.

hep-lat.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
hep-lat.author: Jinzi Wu, Michael Döring, Maxim Mai
hep-lat.abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

hep-lat.title: Heavy-Meson Bag Parameters using Gradient Flow
hep-lat.author: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel
hep-lat.abstract: We demonstrate the use of the gradient flow combined with the short flow-time expansion (GF+SFTX) as a renormalization procedure for four-quark operator matrix elements and associated bag parameters relevant to neutral heavy-meson mixing ($\Delta Q=2$) and heavy-meson lifetimes ($\Delta Q=0$). Using six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we calculate for a charm-strange system with physical quark masses flowed bag parameters and match them to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme using perturbative SFTX coefficients up to next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD. We employ a multiscale matching strategy and a renormalization-group improved flow-time evolution which allows for a reliable estimate of systematic uncertainties. For a fictitious neutral $D_s$ meson, we obtain the $\Delta Q=2$ $\overline{\text{MS}}$ bag parameter ${\cal B}^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.7673(123)$, consistent with existing short-distance $D^0$ mixing determinations. For the $\Delta Q=0$ lifetime-ratio operator basis, we find the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ results $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$, $B^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(71)$, $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_1(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon^{\overline{\text{MS}}}_2(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$. We provide conversion formulae to re-express these results for an arbitrary choice of evanescent operators. These results demonstrate that GF+SFTX can deliver precise determinations of dimension-six four-quark operators and establish a framework for future lattice computations including more complex operator bases, where the challenge of power-divergent mixing is shifted to the continuum and handled in the SFTX.

hep-lat.title: Higher Mellin Moments of the Unpolarized PDF of the Pion and the Kaon from Lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Constantia Alexandrou(Univ. of Cyprus and The Cyprus Inst.), Simone Bacchio(The Cyprus Inst.), Priyajit Jana(Univ. of Cyprus and The Cyprus Inst.), Marcus Petschlies(Univ. of Bonn), Luis Alberto Rodriguez Chacon(The Cyprus Inst. and Univ. of Ferrara), Gregoris Spanoudes(Univ. of Cyprus), Fernanda Steffens(Univ. of Bonn), Carsten Urbach(Univ. of Bonn), Urs Wenger(Univ. of Bern)
hep-lat.abstract: We present results on the Mellin moments of the unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) of the pion and kaon up to the fourth order. The computation is done using one $N_f=2+1+1$ gauge ensemble of twisted mass fermions with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical values. We reconstruct the valence pion and kaon PDFs using the connected contributions to the three Mellin moments. We compare our results on the Mellin moments and the reconstructed PDFs with other lattice QCD and phenomenological determinations.

hep-lat.title: Stochastic Path Sampler For Lattice Field Theory
hep-lat.author: Shiyang Chen, Moxian Qian, Gert Aarts, Biagio Lucini, Kai Zhou
hep-lat.abstract: In lattice field theory, target distributions are known only up to normalization, (\tilde{\pi}(\phi)\propto e^{-S(\phi)}), while the partition function is intractable. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations often become inefficient near phase transitions or the continuum limit due to critical slowing down. In this work, we propose a novel sampler based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, called Stochastic Path Sampler (SPS), which can generate configurations for the unnormalized target distribution without requiring training data. The central idea of SPS is to establish a trajectory-level balance for learnable forward and backward stochastic dynamics between two equilibrium states, namely the prior and target distributions. This is achieved by minimizing the path-space variational free energy, equivalently an entropy-production upper bound, defined by the log-ratio of forward and auxiliary backward trajectory measures, thereby enhancing the reversibility of the forward and backward processes. The learned forward process provides independent proposals, which are subsequently corrected by an extended-space Independence Metropolis--Hastings step. In two-dimensional (\phi^4) theory, we demonstrate that our neural sampler can achieve the same sampling quality as HMC but with a much shorter autocorrelation time in the critical region. This sampler offers a stochastic-quantization-inspired route to data-free proposal construction for lattice field theory by leveraging a variational free-energy principle derived from path-space irreversibility.

hep-lat.title: Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge
hep-lat.author: Xiaojun Yao
hep-lat.abstract: We study quantum simulation of SU(3) non-Abelian gauge theory dynamically coupled with fundamental fermions in $3+1$ dimensions by employing the lattice Hamiltonian in axial gauge under fixed boundary conditions, which avoids Gauss's law constraints. The temporal component of the gauge field is analytically solved in terms of independent field degrees of freedom and a lattice regulated Green's function. The axial gauge condition is trivially maintained in time evolution, even under Trotterization. The gauge field degrees of freedom are expressed in the local field basis and can be efficiently transformed into the canonical conjugate momentum basis by local quantum Fourier transforms. We prove the number of qubits needed for describing all states up to an energy $E$ with an accuracy $\epsilon$ on a lattice of volume $V$ at bare coupling $g$ is bounded as $16n_A V + 12n_f V$, where $n_A \approx \log_2 (\frac{64 E' V^{4/3}}{\pi^2\epsilon} + \frac{32\sqrt{2}g n_f E'^{1/2} V^{7/6}}{\sqrt{3}\pi^3\epsilon^{1/2}} ) $ is the number of qubits needed for each independent gauge field per site with a shifted energy $E'$, and $n_f$ denotes the number of fermion flavors. We then analyze a quantum algorithm for time evolution that is based on Trotterization, quantum Fourier transform, and Jordan-Wigner transformation, for which quantum circuits can be explicitly constructed under arbitrary gauge field truncation and digitization. We find the numbers of CNOT and single-qubit rotation gates scale as $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3}) + O(V^{5/3})$ and $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3})$, respectively, per Trotter step for fixed $n_f\leq 6$. Together with the bounded Trotterization error, we conclude that quantum resources needed for simulating real-time dynamics of lattice QCD scale polynomially with volume, energy, time, accuracy, and bare Hamiltonian parameters.

hep-lat.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
hep-lat.author: Xiaolin Wang, Xingyu Guo, Jinyang Li, Tianyin Li, Enke Wang, Lingxiao Wang, Hongxi Xing
hep-lat.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

hep-lat.title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$-symmetric Point
hep-lat.author: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel
hep-lat.abstract: We calculate the dimension-six $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme with perturbative short flow-time expansion coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to $\tau(D_s)/\tau(D^0)$ at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$ symmetric point, we obtain $B_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$,$B_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(70)$, $\epsilon_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$ using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path towards higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.

hep-lat.title: Finite size scaling of bitstring probability distributions for Rydberg arrays
hep-lat.author: Zane Ozzello, Avi Kaufman, Yannick Meurice
hep-lat.abstract: We calculate the probabilities $p_{\{n\}}$ of the measured bitstrings $\{n\}$ for the vacuum of Rydberg ladders with $N_q$ atoms. As $N_q$ increases, the $p_{\{n\}}$ decrease but become more dense in the low $p$ region, raising the possibility that their smallness could be compensated by their large number. The importance of the low probability states can be estimated from the cumulative probability distribution $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$, which is the probability to observe any state having a probability $p\leq p_{\Lambda}$. For not too large values of $p_{\Lambda}$, it is possible to approximately collapse the $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$ for successive $N_q$ into a function that resembles the Fermi function when plotted as a function of $-\ln(p_{\Lambda})$. We show that the number of shots necessary to reduce $\Sigma(p_{\Lambda},N_q)$ to a sufficiently low value grows exponentially with $N_q$. We discuss the implications for calculating observables associated with the vacuum. We show how the accuracy of these observables may or may not be robust against the number of shots. The collapsed probabilities occur in other systems, where they typically are on one side of the phase transition, in a basis dependent way.

hep-lat.title: Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin $B$-Meson Decays
hep-lat.author: Yong-Kang Huang, Yu-Ming Wang, Xue-Chen Zhao
hep-lat.abstract: We compute for the first time the subleading twist correction to the exclusive rare $b \to \left \{s, d \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays from the three-particle $B$-meson distribution amplitude at next-to-leading order accuracy by employing the soft-collinear effective theory. This constitutes the last missing ingredient for the complete factorization analysis of the hadronic matrix element of the weak effective Hamiltonian at leading power in the heavy quark expansion. Incorporating further a variety of the next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the spectator-scattering amplitude and the weak annihilation topology, we then present the improved field-theoretic predictions for phenomenologically interesting observables in the electroweak penguin $B \to \left \{K, \pi \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays.

hep-lat.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
hep-lat.author: Ioanna Kourkoulou, David Tong
hep-lat.abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.

hep-th.title: When Nonlocal Total Derivatives Are Not Variationally Trivial
hep-th.author: Carlos Heredia
hep-th.abstract: We study total time derivatives in infinite-order and nonlocal Lagrangian mechanics. In the formal infinite-order setting, such terms remain variationally trivial. For nonlocal functionals on trajectories, however, exactness in the form $L=DW$ is not sufficient to ensure a vanishing nonlocal Euler-Lagrange expression. We exhibit a smooth convolution-type counterexample.

hep-th.title: Galilean cosmologies in two dimensions
hep-th.author: Daniel Grumiller, Kai-Yu Zhang
hep-th.abstract: Inspired by Carroll black holes, we consider the most general theory of Galilean dilaton gravity in two dimensions. We find generically that the solution space describes cosmological spacetimes. From a limiting perspective, these Galilean geometries connect the white and black hole singularities through the bifurcation surface. The latter turns into a Galilean extremal surface in the limit of infinite speed of light. We also discuss aspects of Galilean tachydynamics and find that the entropy is given by the dilaton evaluated at the Galilean extremal surface.

hep-th.title: A cubic closed string field theory
hep-th.author: Harold Erbin
hep-th.abstract: The action of closed bosonic string field theory is non-polynomial, and for more than thirty years a no-go theorem of Sonoda and Zwiebach (1990) has excluded a cubic formulation with a single string field, a symmetric vertex and the canonical propagator. We evade it with a Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation and provide an explicit construction of a cubic closed string field theory at all orders. The transformation introduces an infinite tower of auxiliary $k$-string fields $\Sigma_k$, entering at order $g_s^{2 k - 2}$, which turn the vertices with four or more legs into kinetic terms and cubic couplings. The action is cubic, at most quadratic in each auxiliary field, and triangular: eliminating the auxiliary fields by Gaussian integrals recovers the original action order by order at tree level, under invertibility and kernel conditions on the auxiliary kinetic operators. The original gauge symmetry lifts to the cubic action with no new parameter, and we argue that the auxiliary fields add no physical state at generic momentum, wherever their kinetic operators are invertible. On the worldsheet, $\Sigma_2$ is an entangled two-string state: by an operator product expansion, the quartic form reduces to a gluing of two asymmetric cubic vertices dressed by the motion of the local coordinates and defined on states without level matching. We expect this picture to generalize to higher orders, defining a gluing of patches carrying $k$ punctures each. The string vertices, read as products with several outputs, satisfy an extended form of the genus-zero $\mathrm{IBL}_\infty$ relations, including operations with no input or no output, exactly when the string products form a cyclic $L_\infty$ algebra. Finally, we compare our action with the bar--cobar construction of Chiaffrino, Mamade and Zwiebach.

hep-th.title: Anatomy of AdS black hole on-shell actions
hep-th.author: Junho Hong, Sourav Roychowdhury
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the regularized on-shell actions of rotating electrically charged AdS black holes of gauged supergravity via holographic renormalization and background subtraction, with a particular emphasis on the frame in which the radial cutoff is placed. For holographic renormalization, the asymptotically global AdS frame, recently employed in seven dimensions, works equally well in five and six dimensions: the renormalized on-shell action of the AdS$_d$ black holes with $S^1\times S^{d-2}$ conformal boundaries satisfies the quantum statistical relation, up to a parameter-independent Casimir term in odd dimensions, and thereby places the holographic comparisons that so far relied on this relation on a first-principles footing. Background subtraction, in contrast, fails to reproduce this result in the same frame; the mismatch, which we identify exactly in terms of the Casimir term and the counterterms, demands a criterion for the cutoff surface yet to be established. For precision holography, our results settle the choice of frame for holographic renormalization with conformally flat boundaries and delineate the ambiguities that remain in background subtraction and in holographic renormalization for boundaries that are not conformally flat.

hep-th.title: Time Advances and Dispersive Constraints in Dressed Gravitational Scattering
hep-th.author: Ziyu Dong
hep-th.abstract: We derive a low energy group time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering at leading eikonal order with full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile of finite soft scale. Dispersive matching of nonnegative absorption excludes the amplitude's analytic crossing with high energy boundedness. This reflects internal scales growing with energy via string diffusion in quantum gravity and high energy nonlinear graviton rescattering, coupled to soft clouds beyond leading soft order. Interference preserving joint detection of hard particles and coherent soft radiation may reveal the advance.

hep-th.title: Self-gravitating spinning mesonic tubes
hep-th.author: Alex Giacomini, Marcela Lagos, Seung Hun Oh, Aldo Vera
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we construct new self-gravitating solutions for the four-dimensional $SU(2)$ Einstein non-linear sigma model and the Einstein-Skyrme model, both minimally coupled to the Maxwell field, which describes spinning pulsed mesonic tubes. These solutions are gyratonic in the sense that they are characterized by a propagation axis and possess angular momentum. The gyratonic solutions are described by a smooth matter distribution, which is free of curvature singularities. The maximum of the energy density is concentrated on a tube around the propagation axis. We first consider the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to General Relativity and the Maxwell field, constructing asymptotically flat, spinning, pulsed gyratonic solutions. Subsequently, we include the Skyrme term in the analysis. In this case, we show that in order to maintain the resolvability of the matter field equations, the spacetime must be asymptotically de Sitter. It is also shown that, despite the fact that the total topological charge is zero, these solutions possess a non-zero topological charge density.

hep-th.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
hep-th.author: Dmitry Galakhov
hep-th.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

hep-th.title: Casimir Attraction and Repulsion in a Magnetic Domain-Wall Background
hep-th.author: Inés Cavero-Peláez, Beatriz Gómez-López, Jose M. Muñoz-Castañeda, Gonzalo Sancho-Garrido
hep-th.abstract: We study the one-loop Casimir interaction between two $\delta$--$\delta'$ plates in the fixed one-soliton Pöschl--Teller background of the sine-Gordon kink. The transverse fluctuation problem is the Gaussian truncation of an $S^2$ sigma model, equivalently an easy-axis antiferromagnet with a domain wall, in which the plates exert no classical force on the wall. For $v\ge2|w|$ the fluctuation operators are non-negative, and strictly stable couplings, $v>2|w|$, also exclude zero modes, so the quadratic field theory is consistent at the fixed sine-Gordon mass. The background-dressed relative determinant factorises exactly into effective, gradient-dependent strengths of the two plates, and the sign of each frequency channel of the interaction energy is fixed by their orientation. Two identical, equally oriented, strictly stable plates switch from attraction near the kink to repulsion away from it under a rigid translation at fixed couplings and separation. The interaction energy and the force conjugate to the separation neither share their sign everywhere nor change sign at the same positions: there are regions of negative energy and repulsive force, so attraction and repulsion must be read from the force. For such plates with $w\neq0$ the force is repulsive at short and attractive at large separation, and the interaction energy has a minimum at a separation that depends on the position of the pair. For $v=1.05$, $w=0.5$ and $d=1.5$ the energy changes sign at $c\simeq-0.44$ and $2.63$, and the force at $c\simeq-0.30$ and $2.00$.

hep-th.title: Solving spectral flow in AdS$_3$: from covering maps to pencils
hep-th.author: Sergio Iguri, Nicolas Kovensky, Julian H. Toro
hep-th.abstract: Strings in AdS$_3$ with pure NS-NS flux are described by the exactly solvable SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$) WZW model, yet correlators of winding strings, given by spectrally flowed operators, were so far known only up to three points. We obtain all of them, for any number of insertions and windings, in terms of unflowed correlators, proving the four-point conjecture of Dei and Eberhardt. The key ingredient is a pencil of rational maps from the worldsheet to the boundary which exists for generic insertion points, unwinds all insertions at once, and collapses to the covering map when the latter exists.

hep-th.title: Solitons of the intermediate long wave equation with residue source
hep-th.author: Yuto Ishii, Atsushi Nakamula, Soma Yoshida
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the bilinear formulation of the intermediate long-wave (ILW) equation by interpreting its principal-value integrals in the framework of Sato hyperfunctions. When the tau-functions have no zeros inside the relevant contours, the conventional source-free ILW equation is recovered. When zeros enter the contours, their residue contributions must instead be retained, leading naturally to a residue-extended ILW system with self-consistent sources determined by the tau-functions themselves. We introduce a residue index that counts the zeros enclosed in each analytic strip and use it to classify the resulting soliton sectors. The conventional elevation-soliton belongs to the zero-residue sector, whereas depression-solitons and higher elevation branches generally carry non-zero residue indices. Exact one- and multisoliton tau-functions are constructed, including mixed elevation--depression configurations with factorised two-body interactions. Their residue indices are additive and remain invariant during collisions, provided that no zero crosses a contour boundary. A Fourier-space analysis shows that the soliton spectra decay exponentially at large wavenumbers, with a decay rate determined by the distance of the nearest complex singularity from the real axis. This rate vanishes as an odd-multiple boundary between adjacent residue sectors is approached, providing a direct spectral signature of the transition between them.

hep-th.title: $n$-Gon Correlators in $d$-dimensions
hep-th.author: Yong-Xiang Su, Dongyu Yang
hep-th.abstract: We study the analytic structure of scalar one-loop cosmological $n$-gon correlators using an integrand-level reduction and a Baikov representation adapted to linear tube-energy denominators. At spatial dimension $d=n$, we determine the algebraic factors that normalize their local leading singularities to unity and construct explicit $d\log$ forms for arbitrary $n$. For the complete box at $d=n=4$, we evaluate an external-energy discontinuity in a collinear kinematic family and find a nonvanishing complete elliptic integral of the second kind after summing all time orderings. We also compare successive tube-energy discontinuities in $d=3$ and $d=4$, and relate selected tube cuts to the cosmological dressing representation. These results illustrate the importance of integration domains in determining the analytic structure beyond local leading singularities.

hep-th.title: Canonical Commutation Relations and Poisson Brackets with Non-locality in Time
hep-th.author: Yasu Gen, Hiroaki Matsunaga, Jojiro Totsuka
hep-th.abstract: We study the canonical structure of a string-inspired model in which the kinetic term couples fields at times separated by a finite shift $\sigma$, with a coupling $\lambda$ to a fixed background. From the boundary term in the variation of the action, we construct a conserved symplectic form and derive the positive-time Poisson bracket. Using the Schwinger--Dyson relation, we show that at positive time separation $s$ the commutator equals $i\hbar$ times this bracket. The canonical normalization $\hbar$ appears as a jump of the commutator expectation value at $s=\sigma$, which is equal time for shifted variables with a local kinetic term; for $0<s<\sigma$ the commutator vanishes for every $\lambda>0$. Hence $\lambda\to0$ at fixed $\sigma$ does not reproduce the free commutator on this interval, whereas $\sigma\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$ recovers the local commutator at every fixed $s>0$.

hep-th.title: Simplicity of the Three-Loop Six-Point ABJM Amplitude
hep-th.author: Hanyu Fang, Chia-Kai Kuo, Kai Yan
hep-th.abstract: We compute the three-loop six-point amplitude in planar ABJM theory using negative geometries. At this order, only a single bipartite chain contributes to the logarithm of the amplitude, and we find that its dual-conformally invariant integrand is locally finite. The integrated chain is therefore infrared finite and, remarkably, equals exactly $-\pi^2$ times the one-loop amplitude. Hence the collinear anomalous dimension, like the cusp, receives no three-loop correction. Restoring the disconnected products of lower-loop contributions, which carry all the infrared divergences, we obtain the full three-loop amplitude, fixed entirely by lower-loop data and the coefficient $-\pi^2$. These results reveal an unexpected simplicity of the six-point ABJM amplitude and suggest an iterative relation between its odd- and even-loop terms.

hep-th.title: D(-1)/D7 bound states in supergravity
hep-th.author: Gongrui Cheng, Klaas Parmentier, Thomas Van Riet
hep-th.abstract: We construct D($-$1)/D7 bound states in Euclidean type IIB supergravity motivated by the string-theory setup of Billò et al., whose open-string description realizes instantons in eight-dimensional super Yang--Mills theory. Previous supergravity constructions either left unresolved issues concerning ten-dimensional Euclidean supersymmetry or relied on partial smearing to codimension one. We classify the local codimension-two solutions by showing that the supersymmetric field equations reduce to two holomorphic functions subject to a single complex constraint. The candidate bound-state solutions require complementary D3-brane fluxes, consistent with the D7 worldvolume analysis. A particularly interesting solution has constant dilaton and connects the vacuum at infinity to a controlled scaling limit in which the geometry becomes $\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb T^8$.

hep-th.title: A ménage à quatre without strings attached
hep-th.author: Iosif Bena, Gongrui Cheng, Klaas Parmentier, Dimitrios Toulikas, Thomas Van Riet
hep-th.abstract: When two D-branes with eight mixed Dirichlet-Neumann directions cross, a fundamental string is created. This is the Hanany-Witten (HW) effect. In supergravity, the string shows up as an electric NSNS B-field sourced by the RR fields of the two branes. We show that two brane pairs, each of which would create an HW string on its own, can combine into a quadruple bound state with no HW strings attached. We explicitly construct a background with the fluxes of such a D0-D8-D4-D4' quadruple. Requiring no HW strings imposes a quadratic relation among the fluxes. We also realize this bound state as a supersymmetric solution of the non-Abelian DBI action of the D8-branes, whose Killing spinors match those of the bulk supergravity solution. The fluxed D8 stack acts as a domain wall between two supersymmetric D0-D8-D4-D4' backgrounds. Each background satisfies the no-string constraint, and the jumps in the fluxes give the charges carried by the stack.

hep-th.title: Spectra and Central Charges of Gauged Curvature Squared Supergravities in Five Dimensions
hep-th.author: Erol Aksoy, Cagatay Okyay, Mehmet Ozkan, Cemal Berfu Senisik
hep-th.abstract: We study the spectra and the central charges of off-shell gauged five-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supergravity extended by the Weyl squared, Ricci tensor squared and Ricci scalar squared invariants, and by their Gauss-Bonnet combination. Working exactly in the couplings and keeping all auxiliary fields, we organize the spectra around the maximally supersymmetric AdS$_5$ vacuum into supermultiplets. With the Ricci scalar squared invariant, the spectrum gains a long vector multiplet and is free of ghosts in a finite range of the coupling, while with the Weyl squared or Ricci tensor squared invariant, it gains a long spin-2 multiplet and always contains ghosts or instabilities. The Gauss-Bonnet combination adds no new modes: around its supersymmetric vacuum, the quadratic action is a rescaled copy of that of the two-derivative theory, and this fixes the spectrum of the Ricci tensor squared extension. We also compute the central charges $a$ and $c$ and the flavor central charge exactly in the couplings. The vacuum equation is $a$-maximization, and the kinetic terms of the massless graviton and vector multiplets are proportional to $c$ and to the flavor central charge, so that the critical points, where the massive spin-2 multiplet becomes degenerate with the graviton multiplet, are zeros of $c$. Finally, around supersymmetric AdS$_3\times\Sigma_2$ backgrounds of the Gauss-Bonnet extension, the two-dimensional central charges are reproduced by $c$-extremization, while the spectrum is generically not unitary and contains towers of states whose energies stay bounded at large Kaluza-Klein levels. In part of the parameter space, the tower of spin-2 multiplets has positive norm, so that the spectrum has no finite density of states.

hep-th.title: Radiation from scattering on multiple shockwaves
hep-th.author: Tim Adamo, Anton Ilderton, Hannah Kingham
hep-th.abstract: It is well known that radiation produced by scattering an electron off multiple sources depends on the length of the mean free path between these scatterings. When this is sufficiently small, the spectrum is suppressed due to destructive interference, a famous result known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. This is usually modelled approximately, with scattering centres treated linearly (e.g., as screened Coulomb potentials), high-energy probes and soft emitted photons. In this paper, we consider a scenario where multiple scatterings can be computed exactly: charged probe scattering on multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves. Here, the amplitudes for elastic scattering and single photon emission can be determined exactly, for arbitrary kinematics, in terms of the shock profiles in the transverse plane. We use these amplitudes to compute the radiation density (doubly-averaged over shock locations in the transverse plane and lightfront time) in the regimes of independent and interfering scatterings. For shock profiles which are radially symmetric in the transverse plane (including the ultraboosted Coulomb field), we recover the known LPM suppression, albeit with more general kinematics. In addition, our setup allows us to consider the source-free case of multiple scattering on impulsive/ultra-short plane waves, where we find much stronger suppression of the spectrum in the LPM regime.

hep-th.title: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
hep-th.author: Saad Eddine Baddis, Adil Belhaj, Hajar Belmahi, Yassine Hassouni, Maryem Jemri
hep-th.abstract: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.

hep-th.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
hep-th.author: Jie Gu
hep-th.abstract: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

hep-th.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
hep-th.author: Kazumi Okuyama
hep-th.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|\Pi|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.

hep-th.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
hep-th.author: Stefan A. Kurlyand, Arkady A. Tseytlin
hep-th.abstract: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.

hep-th.title: Schwinger-Unruh Interplay and Mode-Resolved Entanglement of Charged Scalar Fields in Rindler Spacetime
hep-th.author: Shagun Kaushal, Himanshu Parihar
hep-th.abstract: We study pairwise and cross-horizon correlations of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime in the presence of parallel electric and magnetic fields. The transverse magnetic field produces Landau levels, while the longitudinal mode problem follows the charged-scalar Rindler construction with the effective mass $M_n^2=m^2+(2n+1)|qB|$. For a specified global vacuum in the negative-frequency sector, we obtain the outgoing four-mode Gaussian state and calculate logarithmic negativity and quantum mutual information for selected mode pairs. We find that the cross-wedge antiparticle-particle pair is entangled only when $q_2<\tanh r_U$. It can therefore become separable although its mutual information remains nonzero. The intra-wedge particle-antiparticle pair remains entangled for nonzero Schwinger squeezing. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. We discuss the Landau-level dependence and the limits of these mode-resolved conclusions, without identifying the vacuum-dependent mixing parameter with a detector temperature.

hep-th.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
hep-th.author: Yu Shi, Sheng Long
hep-th.abstract: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate numerical comparisons, some protocols reach a given tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. To examine the limits of preparation, we consider critical states that already carry a slow scalar field and exterior charge. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of $O(\varepsilon^4)$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient connects this reserve to the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow tail on the normal side. This limited reserve constrains how quickly the existing field can be removed. For releases that suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge, the preparation time grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$ under horizon regularity and uniform radial control.
