Equivalently, it can arise in systems of bosons with particle-hole symmetry, as a long-range-ordered transition point between two quasi-long-range-ordered superfluids. Our approach is to start with the continuum field theory of the isotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet and consider generic perturbations that respect easy-plane symmetry. We argue for a renormalization-group flow to a critical point where long-range order in $(S^x, S^y)$ is enabled by coexisting critical fluctuations of $S^z$. (We also discuss multicritical points where further parameters are tuned to zero.) These results show that it is much easier to break continuous symmetries in 1D than standard lore would suggest. The failure of standard intuition for 1D chains (based on the quantum--classical correspondence) can be attributed to Berry phases, which prevent the 1+1D system from mapping to a classical 2D spin model. The present theory also gives an example of an ordered state whose Goldstone mode is interacting even in the infra-red, rather than becoming a free field.

hep-th.title: A model of errors in transformers
hep-th.author: Suvrat Raju, Praneeth Netrapalli
hep-th.abstract: We study the error rate of LLMs on tasks like arithmetic that require a deterministic output, and repetitive processing of tokens drawn from a small set of alternatives. We argue that incorrect predictions arise when small errors in the attention mechanism accumulate to cross a threshold, and use this insight to derive a quantitative two-parameter relationship between the accuracy and the complexity of the task. The two parameters vary with the prompt and the model; they can be interpreted in terms of an elementary noise rate, and the number of plausible erroneous tokens that can be predicted. Our analysis is inspired by an ``effective field theory'' perspective: the LLM's many raw parameters can be reorganized into just two parameters that govern the error rate. We perform extensive empirical tests, using Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek R1, and find excellent agreement between the predicted and observed accuracy for a variety of tasks, although we also identify deviations in some cases. Our model provides an alternative to suggestions that errors made by LLMs on long repetitive tasks indicate the ``collapse of reasoning'', or an inability to express ``compositional'' functions. Finally, we show how to construct prompts to reduce the error rate.

hep-th.title: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
hep-th.author: Laura Iacconi, David Mulryne, David Seery
hep-th.abstract: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $\delta N$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $\delta N$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.

hep-th.title: When does a lattice higher-form symmetry flow to a topological higher-form symmetry at low energies?
hep-th.author: Ruizhi Liu, Pok Man Tam, Ho Tat Lam, Liujun Zou
hep-th.abstract: We study the lattice version of higher-form symmetries on tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Interestingly, at low energies, these symmetries may not flow to the topological higher-form symmetries familiar from relativistic quantum field theories, but instead to non-topological higher-form symmetries. We present concrete lattice models exhibiting this phenomenon. One particular model is an $\mathbb{R}$ generalization of the Kitaev honeycomb model featuring an $\mathbb{R}$ lattice 1-form symmetry. We show that its low-energy effective field theory is a gapless, non-relativistic theory with a non-topological $\mathbb{R}$ 1-form symmetry. In both the lattice model and the effective field theory, we demonstrate that the non-topological $\mathbb{R}$ 1-form symmetry is not robust against local perturbations. In contrast, we also study various modifications of the toric code and their low-energy effective field theories to demonstrate that the compact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice 1-form symmetry does become topological at low energies unless the Hamiltonian is fine-tuned. Along the way, we clarify the rules for constructing low-energy effective field theories in the presence of multiple superselection sectors. Finally, we argue on general grounds that non-compact higher-form symmetries (such as $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ 1-form symmetries) in lattice systems generically remain non-topological at low energies, whereas compact higher-form symmetries (such as $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ and $U(1)$ 1-form symmetries) generically become topological.

hep-th.title: A Generalized Landauer's Principle for Unitarily Transformed Thermal Reservoirs
hep-th.author: Hao Xu
hep-th.abstract: Landauer's principle, a cornerstone of quantum information and thermodynamics, appears to be violated when the thermal reservoir is replaced by a squeezed thermal state (STS), owing to the additional thermodynamic resources inherently present in the squeezed state. We introduce a formal extension of the principle to such unitarily transformed thermal states. By defining an effective Hamiltonian, we rigorously establish a generalized Landauer inequality, which naturally reduces to the standard case for an ordinary thermal reservoir as a special instance. The framework further yields a consistent definition of entropy production and a proof of its non-negativity. We illustrate its utility by studying an arbitrarily moving Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a quantum field initially prepared in the STS. Using perturbation theory, we compute the entropy production explicitly, confirming its positivity. As a result of the symmetry breaking induced by the unitary transformation, it depends on both the proper time interval and the absolute spacetime position. Our work clarifies the apparent violation of Landauer's principle with STSs by providing a consistent information-theoretic framework. It also offers a practical tool for computing entropy production in non-equilibrium and relativistic settings, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines and information protocols.

hep-th.title: Nonperturbative Resummation of Divergent Time-Local Generators: Disentangling Non-Markovian Dynamics
hep-th.author: Dragomir Davidovic
hep-th.abstract: Perturbative van Kampen cumulant expansions of time-local generators of open quantum systems generically diverge at long times, while the reduced dynamics remains regular. We show that these divergences encode information sufficient to reconstruct an approximate nonperturbative dynamical map. Although their resummation remains divergent, disentangling the dynamics according to its van Hove limit resolves the divergence and exposes its dynamical origin: the map approaches isolated times at which it becomes noninvertible. For the weak-coupling unbiased spin--boson model, the reconstructed non-Markovian dynamics takes the disentangled form \begin{equation*} \Phi=\Phi_{\mathrm{GAD}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{NS}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{Khal}}, \end{equation*} separating generalized amplitude damping, exponentially damped nonsecular coherence mixing, and a projective, phase-selective Khalfin map. Thus, the onset of recurrent noninvertibility is the reduced-dynamical-map manifestation of the Khalfin transition from exponential to algebraic relaxation. Although the coherences acquire algebraic Khalfin tails, the distinguishability of quantum superposition states remains governed by an exponential decay law well after the Khalfin transition. Comparison with numerically exact TEMPO dynamics validates the procedure and shows that apparently complex non-Markovian dynamics can resolve into a small number of distinct, physically transparent dynamical processes.

hep-th.title: How acausal equations emerge from causal dynamics
hep-th.author: Lorenzo Gavassino
hep-th.abstract: We construct a causal and covariantly stable kinetic model whose spectrum at real wavenumbers $k$ reproduces any rest-frame stable dissipative dispersion relation $\omega(k)$ via suitable initialization of the microscopic degrees of freedom. Macroscopic observables can therefore obey arbitrary linear evolution equations (including forms that would be acausal if taken as fundamental), while the underlying dynamics remains causal, and all apparent propagation is encoded in the initial data. This provides an explicit counterexample to the idea that microscopic causality alone constrains the analytic form of dispersion relations at real $k$. In particular, bounds on transport coefficients based solely on the analytic structure of $\omega(k)$, such as the hydrohedron bounds, require additional assumptions about the region in the complex $k$-plane where $\omega(k)$ corresponds to physical modes.

hep-th.title: The Vacuum Displacement Principle: Theoretical Framework and Local Phenomenology
hep-th.author: Rodrigo Maier
hep-th.abstract: We present a modified gravitational framework in which the standard Einstein field equations are sourced by a classical matter sector coupled to a Higgs-type scalar field $\chi$ modeling a dynamic vacuum substrate. By introducing a phenomenological covariant coupling we implement a physical displacement principle where massive baryonic matter drives the vacuum field away from its vacuum expectation value. We show that this coupling leads to a field-dependent modulation of a particle's inertial rest mass alongside a spatial fifth force, yielding localized violations of the Einstein Equivalence Principle while preserving universal free fall for fundamental point masses. In the weak-field, non-relativistic limit, this interaction manifests as a Yukawa-type correction to the Newtonian potential. We test the viability of this framework against local gravitational constraints, including planetary perihelion precession and Eötvös parameter limits. Finally, we model the steady-state, non-relativistic spherical accretion of dust, demonstrating that the competing effects of vacuum-induced mass modulation and fifth-force acceleration yield distinct density and velocity profiles.

hep-th.title: Heavy Quark Transport is Non-Gaussian Beyond Leading Log
hep-th.author: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld
hep-th.abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has asymmetric exponential tails that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.

hep-th.title: A reason why we do not observe Schrödinger's cats
hep-th.author: Fabio Siringo
hep-th.abstract: A reason is discussed (may be not the only one) for why we do not see any superposition of macroscopic states in the real world. Under the general assumption that quantum macrostates are statistical ensembles of microstates, it is shown that any superposition of macrostates is reduced in a very short time by the unitary dynamics of the ordinary Schrödinger equation, deducing the Born rule without having to postulate it. In more detail, the macroscopic and microscopic degrees of freedom are decoupled in the Schrödinger equation, yielding an effective stochastic equation for the macroscopic variables, with the ensemble average of the microscopic amplitudes that acts as a self-generated internal white noise. The stochastic equation is shown to be a reducing Itô equation if some general causality conditions are met, predicting a very quick collapse of any macroscopic superposition upon formation, with probabilities which satisfy the Born rule. In the context of the von Neumann measurement scheme, the relevance of the result is discussed as a simple dynamical solution of the measurement problem.

hep-th.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
hep-th.author: Xijia Miao
hep-th.abstract: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.

hep-th.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
hep-th.author: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu
hep-th.abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

hep-th.title: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
hep-th.author: Han Lai, Atsuhisa Ota
hep-th.abstract: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_\tau h_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.

hep-th.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
hep-th.author: Ch. M. Benavides, C. S. Muñoz, B. C. Canas, Eduardo Rojas
hep-th.abstract: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_\mu$ and $L_e-L_\tau$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.

hep-th.title: Binary black hole scattering with generic spins
hep-th.author: Adam Clark, Geraint Pratten, Patricia Schmidt
hep-th.abstract: We study generic-spin black-hole scattering with orbital-plane precession, whose dynamics require more than one scattering angle. From numerical relativity (NR), we extract the polar scattering angle and precession of the orbital plane, the latter characterised by asymptotic Euler angles. A dictionary relating post-Minkowskian (PM) observables to scattering and Euler angles is presented, enabling the first precessing PM-NR comparisons. Our results provide a key benchmark for generic-spin resummations and provide the foundations for exploring boundary-to-bound maps in the generic case.

hep-th.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
hep-th.author: Branislav Jurčo, Ján Pulmann, Martin Zika
hep-th.abstract: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.

hep-th.title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
hep-th.author: Hrant Topchyan, Rudik Badalyan, Ara Sedrakyan
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Klümper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $\Delta_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $\Delta_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.

hep-th.title: Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge
hep-th.author: Xiaojun Yao
hep-th.abstract: We study quantum simulation of SU(3) non-Abelian gauge theory dynamically coupled with fundamental fermions in $3+1$ dimensions by employing the lattice Hamiltonian in axial gauge under fixed boundary conditions, which avoids Gauss's law constraints. The temporal component of the gauge field is analytically solved in terms of independent field degrees of freedom and a lattice regulated Green's function. The axial gauge condition is trivially maintained in time evolution, even under Trotterization. The gauge field degrees of freedom are expressed in the local field basis and can be efficiently transformed into the canonical conjugate momentum basis by local quantum Fourier transforms. We prove the number of qubits needed for describing all states up to an energy $E$ with an accuracy $\epsilon$ on a lattice of volume $V$ at bare coupling $g$ is bounded as $16n_A V + 12n_f V$, where $n_A \approx \log_2 (\frac{64 E' V^{4/3}}{\pi^2\epsilon} + \frac{32\sqrt{2}g n_f E'^{1/2} V^{7/6}}{\sqrt{3}\pi^3\epsilon^{1/2}} ) $ is the number of qubits needed for each independent gauge field per site with a shifted energy $E'$, and $n_f$ denotes the number of fermion flavors. We then analyze a quantum algorithm for time evolution that is based on Trotterization, quantum Fourier transform, and Jordan-Wigner transformation, for which quantum circuits can be explicitly constructed under arbitrary gauge field truncation and digitization. We find the numbers of CNOT and single-qubit rotation gates scale as $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3}) + O(V^{5/3})$ and $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3})$, respectively, per Trotter step for fixed $n_f\leq 6$. Together with the bounded Trotterization error, we conclude that quantum resources needed for simulating real-time dynamics of lattice QCD scale polynomially with volume, energy, time, accuracy, and bare Hamiltonian parameters.

hep-th.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
hep-th.author: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou
hep-th.abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.

hep-th.title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
hep-th.author: Yu-Cun Xie, Vaishak Prasad
hep-th.abstract: A new common apparent horizon forms during a binary black hole merger and gives rise to outer and inner branches of marginally outer trapped surfaces. We derive the local structure of these branches. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. The outer and inner common horizons lie on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube along which slice time has a local minimum at formation, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Sufficiently smooth quasilocal scalar functionals with nonzero first variation along the principal zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover the square-root exponent, $1/2$, to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news raises the possibility that common horizon formation has a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.

hep-th.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
hep-th.author: Jonas Loy, Jan C. Louw
hep-th.abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$. Thus $\lambda_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.

hep-th.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
hep-th.author: Jongheon Baek, Gihwan Nam
hep-th.abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.

hep-th.title: Nash Equilibrium from Quantum-Field Entanglement
hep-th.author: Hao Xu
hep-th.abstract: Entanglement harvesting allows localized probes to extract entanglement from a quantum field, even when their interaction regions are spacelike separated. However, how the resource obtained by the probes can be operationalized remains largely open. In this work, we ask whether the harvested entanglement can influence the timing choices of observers acting as players. We construct a quantum input game for Alice and Bob, each controlling an Unruh-DeWitt detector that couples to the vacuum of a free massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. Each player can choose an early interaction time, a late interaction time, or exit. After joint entry, a referee sends independent question qubits, so that fixed local Bell measurements and a payment table convert the detector state into a payoff. The mean payoff is proportional to minus the expectation value of an entanglement witness and is nonpositive for every separable resource. We calculate the detector state to leading perturbative order and solve the participation game analytically. Away from payoff degeneracies, every timing equilibrium with positive payoff gives two trembling hand perfect participation equilibria, in addition to mutual exit. The total count can therefore be one, three, five, or seven. For one fixed switching function and timing menu, five selected delays give the sequence seven, three, one, seven, and one. The timing payoffs follow from the field's two-point functions, with the Hadamard and Pauli-Jordan contributions to the coherence competing against local excitation noise. The resulting equilibrium structure provides an operational setting for studying how vacuum correlations and causal propagation affect the strategic use of quantum-field entanglement.

hep-th.title: Black objects in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime
hep-th.author: Adriano Viganò
hep-th.abstract: We use the Ehlers symmetry of the five-dimensional Ernst equation to embed the Myers-Perry black hole and the rotating black ring in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime. We show that both solutions can be made free of conical singularities, and that the swirl modifies the balance condition of the black ring. We compute horizon areas, surface gravities and Komar charges, which satisfy a Smarr relation, and study the ergoregions.

hep-th.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (II): $[3,-1]$ blocks, VGIT, and toric phases
hep-th.author: Atsushi Kanazawa
hep-th.abstract: We study mirror symmetry for a class of generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau (gCICY) threefolds via variations of GIT. Our focus is on gCICY threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^1\times B$ with a $[3,-1]$ block, cut out by sections of $O(3)\boxtimes O_B(L)$ and $O(-1)\boxtimes O_B(L+R)$, where $B$ is a smooth projective fourfold and $2L+R=-K_B$. Auxiliary variables turn the generalized section into a relative variation of GIT, whose two phases are the gCICY threefold itself and the zero locus of a rank-3 bundle on $\mathbb{P}^2\times B$, and they are isomorphic or related by $\int_B L^4$ disjoint Atiyah flops. Over products of projective spaces, there are 18 Calabi-Yau threefold configurations with a $[3,-1]$ block. All of them except the non-Gorenstein case studied in the companion paper have toric phases with Gorenstein ambient spaces and nef partitions, so that after the variation of GIT their mirror symmetry reduces to Batyrev-Borisov duality. We analyze four examples with a $[3,-1]$ block and one outside this class in detail.

hep-th.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
hep-th.author: Giorgio Galanti
hep-th.abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

hep-th.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
hep-th.author: Arielle Schutz, Ratindranath Akhoury
hep-th.abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation between global modes and modes across the bifurcate Killing horizon of the black hole, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor dependent on the evaporation rate.Next, we discuss the analysis of the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. The entangled global vacuum again has a thermofield double structure. However, we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation.

hep-th.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
hep-th.author: Ferreira Bastien
hep-th.abstract: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.

hep-th.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
hep-th.author: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh
hep-th.abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.

hep-th.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
hep-th.author: Chris D. White
hep-th.abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

hep-th.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
hep-th.author: Samuel Sánchez López, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno Sánchez
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

hep-th.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
hep-th.author: Xiaowei Li, Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

hep-th.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
hep-th.author: Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli
hep-th.abstract:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.05.
